artifacts.title: Tail Certificates and Achievement-Set Geometry for Erdős Problems 249 and 257
artifacts.claim_scope: Gateway exposition for Erdős Problems 249 and 257. For #249 it records the exact dyadic-section rank 2^e+1 for e >= 1, infinite-dimensionality, the explicit finite Farey denominator exclusion, and diagonal certificates through t = 82, but no instance at t = 83 or unbounded family. For #257 it records checked restricted-support geometry and the remaining half-value and 1/21 branches. Both problems remain open, and the shared Lambert-series change of variables transfers no irrationality theorem.

artifacts.title: From Spare Compute to Cumulative Mathematics
artifacts.claim_scope: A strategy and working-prototype paper for an open research commons that accepts compute, mathematical direction, architecture improvements, cold-clone cleanup, and review. It defines role-bounded contribution packets, a candidate-to-attention funnel, provenance-preserving adoption, and evaluation measures. As of 31 August 2026 no completed external cold clone or accepted external contribution had been recorded. All eight Erdős problems remain open; the paper reports no measured discovery-rate improvement, independent mathematical review, proof of optimal architecture, or community acceptance of a new mathematical result.

artifacts.title: The Binary Totient Series
artifacts.claim_scope: Claim-bounded reasoning record for Erdős Problem 249. It distinguishes checked premises and finite certificates from open obligations: the level-e dyadic-section rank is 2^e+1 only for e >= 1; the full span is infinite-dimensional; the finite Farey computation excludes denominators up to the stated bound; and diagonal certificates exist through t = 82, with neither t = 83 nor an unbounded family supplied. Irrationality remains open.

artifacts.title: Reciprocal Mersenne Subseries
artifacts.claim_scope: Claim-bounded reasoning record for Erdős Problem 257. It gives a complete ordinary proof of the finite-prime weighted support criterion, including a support with divergent reciprocal sum, and separately presents checked finite-support and restricted-achievement-set structure and Lean full-support and structured-support theorems. No finite rank-at-least-two support represents 1/21; the primitive 2p+3q cone has the stated coverage and recurrent multiplicities, but the eventual affine-supercapacity regime survives. The universal, half-value, and 1/21 membership questions remain open.

artifacts.title: A Basis for the 2-Kernel of Euler's Totient
artifacts.claim_scope: Standalone exposition of Erdős Problem 249, ordered unconditional results first: the exact level-e dyadic totient section rank 2^e+1 for e >= 1 (Lean) and the resulting infinite-dimensionality, which for integer-valued sequence modules is equivalent to Coons's non-k-regularity and is not an independent contribution; the all-base exact-rank upgrade uses Martin's external independence hypothesis. A separate ordinary argument treats bounded-residue series A_m. The explicit finite-Farey denominator exclusion and Lean diagonal certificates through t = 82 are finite; neither t = 83 nor an unbounded family is supplied. Irrationality remains open.

artifacts.title: Weighted Support Criteria for Reciprocal Mersenne Subseries
artifacts.claim_scope: Standalone exposition of Erdős Problem 257. Full-support irrationality at every integer base b >= 2 is Lean (classical). Structured supports with extra hypotheses — pairwise-coprime plus summable reciprocal mass, and nonnegative eventually-periodic coefficients — are Lean. The finite-prime weighted summability criterion is ordinary mathematics, with a full proof in the long paper. It includes every reciprocal-summable support and some supports with divergent reciprocal sum. A common finite averaging schedule also proves hereditary all-base irrationality for unions of a base-two weighted host and a positive divisor-cover host. These analytic criteria are ordinary and not formalised in this checkout; the proposed hosts separating the classes remain unassessed. Finite-period noncollapse is Lean and concerns finite supports only. Arbitrary infinite support, and the 1/2 and 1/21 branches, remain open and are kept distinct from the full-support and structured-support theorems. Duverney–Tachiya and Tao–Teräväinen are cited, not claimed.

artifacts.title: Two Incomparable Denominator Exclusions\\for $\sum_{n\ge2}(n!-1)^{-1}$
artifacts.claim_scope: Exposition of the ErdosProblems.Erdos68 modules. The Comparator isolation pin for the carry equivalences is FactorialGapPlateauCore; FactorialZeroPlateau is the default-root duplicate of that family, not the isolation source. Lean checks the exact factorial-successor and eventual-unit-carry frontiers, integral-channel and prime-translator identities, weighted projection consumers, and the Cramer residual identity. An independently regenerated exact GMP certificate supplies one non-unit carry at m = 300000, and a Lean theorem consumes that finite fact to exclude every smaller positive rational denominator; a separate continued-fraction bound gives q ≥ 2^39990. The two finite exclusions are incomparable. No theorem supplies cofinally many non-unit carries; Erdős Problem 68 remains open.

artifacts.title: Excluding the Bounded Negative Part
artifacts.claim_scope: Exposition of the ErdosProblems.Erdos243 modules. Lean checks the integer-state bounded-negative theorem, with eventual strict centring, a bounded negative part, and normalised vanishing remaining explicit hypotheses, together with constant- and periodic-negative exclusions. The original-coordinate LCM/product-defect corollary is an ordinary transfer; PaperCompleteR7/ProductDefect.lean is absent from this checkout. Koizumi supplies normalised vanishing for the canonical orbit; boundedness of its negative part is not supplied. Unbounded upward excursions of the unreduced numerator remain open, so Erdős Problem 243 remains open.

artifacts.title: A Countermodel for Growth-and-Parity Arguments\\on the Prime-Gap Dyadic Series
artifacts.claim_scope: Exposition of the ErdosProblems.Erdos251 module. A sparse perturbation of the prime gaps can have a rational dyadic sum while retaining the prime growth scale, every fixed eventual congruence, and asymptotically the same short-block statistics; the later positions are not asserted to be prime. This is complementary to Land's conditional result, not a refutation. Lean checks an elementary pair-and-buffer core; the full schedule and block-law estimates are ordinary mathematics, not Lean- or Comparator-verified. The prime-to-gap identity is the already-known summation-by-parts (Tao on the forum, 7 October 2025); this checkout checks it, discharging summability by an elementary polynomial prime bound rather than the prime-number theorem. Lean also checks unboundedness and non-eventual-periodicity of the actual prime gaps, and the exact local implication from cofinally recurring adjacent small-mismatch tail shifts to failure of eventual integrality. The tail-shift route requires that condition for every fixed positive h; the h=1 case alone does not complete it. No theorem supplies the required cofinal adjacent small-mismatch pairs, and Erdős Problem 251 remains open.

artifacts.title: No Finite Separable Representation\\at Three Prime Generators
artifacts.claim_scope: Steve Fan posted the two-prime factorisation, reduction and transcendence conclusion first (erdosproblems.com/269, 26 June 2026, post-7218). This paper records that argument as an ordinary deduction from Bugeaud–Laurent's external Hecke–Mahler theorem and does not claim priority or a Lean theorem for the two-prime case. For three primes the paper proves nonsingular selected minors of every order from one binary carry. Comparator checks the (2,3,5) minor −1/15, the running-LCM height identity, and a conditional carry-escape consumer; it does not check the arbitrary-order rank theorem. The actual-series reduction is given; the source-specific cofinal escape remains unproved. Problem 269 remains open from three primes onward.

artifacts.title: Sharp Solved Families and\\Constant-Factor Paths in Polynomial Lemniscates
artifacts.claim_scope: This note gives ordinary proofs for explicit short-path families, led by all-degree monic trinomials, and separately establishes a sharp critical-value mean. Lean checks Newton-flow value decay, the exponential first integral, the oriented-ray connection obstruction, the exact common-translation collision locus, finite affine-line avoidance, and root retention under small constant perturbations. Three solved-family kernels (collinear, primitive quintic, translated cubic fibres) are Comparator-checked in ExternalVerification1041SolvedFamilies; they are kernels, not the ordinary length-<2 assemblies. The all-degree trinomial paths, the 13/25 certificate, the Poisson critical-value mean, and the separation/solved-family assemblies that turn kernels into paths are ordinary mathematics. PaperTrinomial.lean is absent. Exact obstruction examples, including a Cassini counterexample to the printed global tree budget of a March 2026 manuscript's Proposition 12, show why those estimates cannot be silently promoted to a general connector theorem. The recent degree-seven counterexample announcement is a separate external claim. Erdős Problem 1041 remains open.

artifacts.title: Irrationality of $F(31/4)$ and the\\Exact Normalized Hankel Order
artifacts.claim_scope: The short-paper headline that F(31/4) and its positive powers are irrational is an ordinary specialization of Zudilin 2004, not a Lean irrationality theorem. Lean checks supporting machinery: the 81/200 height-region arithmetic that places 31/4 inside that region and 3/2 outside, the coordinatewise corridor exclusion at 3/2, the cleared-tail recurrence, and selected Hankel identities (the Lean Hankel-determinant identification does not cover all rows). The outstanding 3/2 obligation is an actual approximant family with remainder control. Universal Erdős #1049 remains open.

artifacts.title: Lemniscates and Newton Flow: Complete Reasoning Record
artifacts.claim_scope: Claim-bounded reasoning record for Erdős Problem 1041. It assembles ordinary all-degree trinomial paths and a sharp critical-value mean, Lean Newton-flow decay, ray separation, translation-collision geometry and root retention, Comparator-checked solved-family kernels, and exact obstructions including the Cassini counterexample to the printed global tree budget. The unrestricted path problem remains open.

artifacts.title: Rational-Base Lambert Series: Complete Reasoning Record
artifacts.claim_scope: Complete reasoning record for Erdős #1049. The region theorem and F(31/4) are ordinary proofs citing Zudilin's Lemma 7; Lean checks finite height comparisons and selected arithmetic, not those irrationality theorems. The exact normalized Hankel order is ordinary with a partial Lean assembly that stops before all rows. The missing 3/2 step is an actual primitive approximation family with nonzero remainder. The problem remains open.

artifacts.title: The Factorial-Denominator Series: Complete Reasoning Record
artifacts.claim_scope: Claim-bounded reasoning record for Erdős #68. Lean checks the Core carry equivalences. The ordinary LCM liminf bound and the finite prime-cancellation examples sit on the common-denominator side of reduction and do not replace the reduced-denominator carry test. The problem remains open.

artifacts.title: Reciprocal-Tail Rigidity: Complete Reasoning Record
artifacts.claim_scope: Complete reasoning record for Erdős #243. The cubic-rate irrationality theorem is ordinary mathematics, including the Chebotarev step, and is not a Lean endpoint. Lean checks the integer-state rigidity results, including a scalar finite-negative-mass criterion. The established bounded-negative regime is distinct from the remaining unbounded upward excursions of the unreduced numerator. The problem remains open.

artifacts.title: Prime Gaps and Dyadic Tails: Complete Reasoning Record
artifacts.claim_scope: Complete reasoning record for Erdős #251. The exact prime-to-gap identity does not use the prime-number theorem. The finite counting reduction for shifted prime-gap differences and the countermodel remain the supported contribution; analytic sieve estimates are not a remaining assumption of the identity. The actual-prime tail witness remains open. The problem remains open.

artifacts.title: The Three-Prime Running LCM: Complete Reasoning Record
artifacts.claim_scope: Complete reasoning record for Erdős #269. The two-prime transcendence argument is Steve Fan's (26 June 2026) and is not a Lean theorem. The three-prime selected-minor obstruction is ordinary paper mathematics and is not Comparator-checked. Comparator names the (2,3,5) minor −1/15, the running-LCM height identity, and a conditional carry-escape consumer. The actual-series reduction is given; the source-specific cofinal escape remains unproved. The problem remains open.
